heading: 4.2 Objective Two: hs-CRP in simple and complicated appendicitis
objective: To assess the diagnostic value of hs-CRP for distinguishing complicated from simple appendicitis.
methods: Histopathology was the reference standard: acute, suppurative, phlegmonous, gangrenous and perforated appendicitis were positive; reactive lymphoid hyperplasia was negative. Simple appendicitis comprised the first three positive categories and complicated appendicitis comprised gangrenous or perforated disease. The analysis included 77 positive specimens: 69 simple and eight complicated cases; all had hs-CRP values. Negative histopathology was excluded from this severity question. The prespecified positive threshold was >3 mg/L. Mann–Whitney U testing was used because the complicated group was small. A rank-biserial effect with a 1,000-bootstrap interval describes the distribution contrast. Wilson intervals describe diagnostic proportions; a stratified 1,000-bootstrap interval describes raw hs-CRP AUC. The Youden-selected threshold is secondary.
finalParagraph: hs-CRP concentrations were higher in complicated appendicitis and showed strong observed severity discrimination. However, >3 mg/L was poorly specific for complication, and the alternative threshold should be treated as a secondary finding requiring validation.
